text: Indian Railways runs more than 13,000 passenger trains every day.
The Chenab Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir is the world's highest railway arch bridge, about 359 metres above the river.
Mawsynram in Meghalaya is often cited as the wettest place on Earth by average rainfall.
Bhutan measures Gross National Happiness and is one of the few carbon-negative countries.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, at about 0.44 square kilometres.
Russia spans 11 time zones.
Lake Baikal in Siberia holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water.
Iceland has no native mosquitoes.
Australia is wider from east to west than the Moon is across.
Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world combined.
Parts of the Grand Trunk Road are over 2,000 years old; it runs from Bangladesh through India and Pakistan to Afghanistan.
The first computer 'bug' was a real moth found in a Harvard Mark II relay in 1947.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed for typewriters in the 1870s.
UPI crossed 10 billion transactions in a single month for the first time in August 2023.
The first text message, sent in 1992, said 'Merry Christmas'.
Ray Tomlinson picked the '@' symbol for email addresses in 1971.
Half a byte, 4 bits, is called a nibble.
The first webcam watched a coffee pot at Cambridge University so people knew when it was full.
'Wi-Fi' doesn't stand for anything; it was a brand name chosen in 1999.
Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the Moon's south pole, in August 2023.
The Python programming language is named after Monty Python, not the snake.
The first iPhone launched in 2007 without an App Store; it arrived a year later.
Sachin Tendulkar is the only player with 100 international centuries.
India won the first T20 World Cup, in 2007.
A men's cricket ball must weigh between 155.9 and 163 grams.
Anil Kumble took all 10 wickets in a Test innings against Pakistan in 1999.
The 1939 'Timeless Test' between South Africa and England was abandoned as a draw after nine days of play so England could catch their ship home.
The Ashes trophy is a tiny urn said to hold the ashes of a burnt bail.
Kapil Dev's India won the 1983 World Cup final at Lord's.
Rohit Sharma holds the highest ODI score, 264, made against Sri Lanka in 2014.
The Indian Premier League began in 2008.
Brian Lara's 400 not out in 2004 is the highest individual score in Test cricket.
A 'duck' comes from 'duck's egg', for the shape of the zero next to a batter's name.
Raja Harishchandra (1913) by Dadasaheb Phalke is considered India's first full-length feature film.
Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge ran at Mumbai's Maratha Mandir for more than 1,000 weeks.
Alam Ara (1931) was India's first sound film.
Lata Mangeshkar recorded songs in more than 30 languages.
Mother India (1957) was India's first submission to the Academy Awards, and it was nominated.
Lagaan (2001) was nominated for the Oscar for Best Foreign Language Film.
'Naatu Naatu' from RRR won the Oscar for Best Original Song in 2023.
Amitabh Bachchan's famous voice was once turned down by All India Radio.
Sholay (1975) was mostly shot in the rocky hills near Ramanagara in Karnataka.
India makes more feature films each year than any other country.
Kishore Kumar had no formal training in music.
In the US, cows kill more people each year than sharks do.
Some 19th-century 'safety coffins' had bells, in case someone was buried alive.
Fredric Baur, who designed the Pringles can, had some of his ashes buried in one.
Thomas Midgley Jr. invented both leaded petrol and CFCs, and died tangled in a pulley system he had built.
Napoleon was once mobbed by a horde of rabbits at a hunt organised in his honour.
Ancient Egyptian embalmers removed the brain through the nose.
In medieval Europe, animals were sometimes put on trial for crimes.
The Great Molasses Flood of 1919 killed 21 people in Boston.
France last used the guillotine in 1977.
Tutankhamun was buried with about 130 walking sticks.
In 1518, dozens of people in Strasbourg danced for days on end in the 'dancing plague'.
Sea otters often hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart.
Cows have preferred companions and are calmer when they're together.
Rats 'laugh' when tickled, at a pitch too high for humans to hear.
Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror.
A border collie named Chaser learned the names of more than 1,000 toys.
Gentoo penguins give pebbles to their partners when building a nest.
Honeybees can learn to recognise human faces.
Crows remember human faces for years.
Squirrels plant thousands of trees by forgetting where they buried their nuts.
Dolphins have signature whistles that work like names.
The Amul girl has starred in topical ads since 1966.
Honey doesn't spoil; edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.
Bananas are slightly radioactive because of the potassium in them.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Water can boil and freeze at the same time, at its triple point.
There are more possible games of chess than atoms in the observable universe.
Sharks have been around longer than trees.
Mangalyaan made India the first country to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt, in 2014.
The Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 cm taller in summer as its iron expands.
A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh around a billion tonnes.
Chicken tikka masala is often said to have been invented in Glasgow.
Light from the Moon takes about 1.3 seconds to reach Earth.
The bhut jolokia from Northeast India was once the world's hottest chilli.
Each cashew nut grows attached to a fruit called the cashew apple.
India is the world's largest producer of milk.
Maggi noodles launched in India in 1983.
Botanically, strawberries aren't berries, but bananas are.
Peanuts aren't nuts; they're legumes, like peas and lentils.
The samosa most likely reached India from Central Asia with traders, centuries ago.
Saffron is the world's most expensive spice by weight.
Tomato ketchup was sold as a medicine in the 1830s.
After water, tea is the most consumed drink in the world.
India's Constitution is the longest written constitution of any country.
The Indian national flag's design is credited to Pingali Venkayya.
Around 970 million people were registered to vote in India's 2024 general election, the largest electorate ever.
Electronic voting machines were first used in India in 1982, in a by-election in Kerala.
India lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 in 1989.
The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved; a third of its members retire every two years.
India's first general election, in 1951-52, took about four months.
The indelible ink used in Indian elections is made by one company, Mysore Paints and Varnish.
New Zealand was the first self-governing country to give women the vote, in 1893.
Switzerland's presidency rotates every year among its seven federal councillors.
The Gir forest once had a polling booth set up for a single voter.
